newsitem.title: CANADA: Rogers margins below industry standards.
newsitem.headline: Rogers margins below industry standards.

text.p: Rogers Communications Inc chief executive Ted Rogers said on Thursday that the company's operating margins are below industry standards and are thus not acceptable to Rogers management.

"While we made much progress during the quarter in a number of areas, our operating margins remain below industry averages and this is unacceptable to operating management and Rogers," Rogers said in a statement.
"As a result, management is focused on improving the Company's operating cost structures and the efficiency of its capital expenditure programs," he added.

Rogers sales rose across the board while operating income climbed modestly. Operating costs in the quarter reflect both the up-front costs of adding cellular subscribers and various investments and initiatives designed to prepare cable for new services and increased competition, he added.

The company said restructuring initiatives in the cable and wireless units in addition to the sales of non-strategic assets unveiled in the quarter show the company is committed to strengthening its financial position.
"They are important first steps in our program to reduce leverage and provide the financial foundation and flexibility for future growth," Rogers said.

In the third quarter of 1996, Rogers revenue was C$628.0 million versus C$554.3 million in the prior-year period. The company said the rise was primarily due to a 21.6 percent increase in wireless revenues and an 8.2 percent rise in cable sales over the 1995 third quarter.
Rogers lost C$0.87 per share, including charges, in the quarter versus a loss of C$0.15 in the 1995 quarter.

Results include a loss from discontinued operations of C$187,000 versus a loss of C$719,000 a year ago. Nine months results include a a gain of C$3,127,000 from discontinued operations and a loss of C$1,511,00 a year ago.

In the third quarter there was a special charge of C$67.4 million for cable restructuring charges. Rogers also incurred a charge of C$20.3 million at Wireless for first operation Time Division Multiple Access digital handsets and for the the exit costs from the closure of Wireless corporate store opeartions.
